chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu Hamza, who said: I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about creation.

He said: When God, Blessed and Exalted, created the creatures from clay, He distributed them like the casting of divination arrows. He brought forth the Muslim and made him fortunate, and made the disbeliever miserable.

Then when the seed (sperm) falls, the angels receive it and give it form, then they say: O Lord, male or female? The Lord — Majestic is His majesty — says: whichever He wills. And they both say: Blessed is God, the Best of Creators!

Then it is placed in her womb and circulates for nine days through every vein and joint. The womb has three locks: a lock at its upper part adjacent to the top of the navel from the right side, another lock at its middle, and another lock at the lower part of the womb.
After nine days it is placed in the upper lock and remains there for three months; during this time the woman is affected by nausea and vomiting.

Then it descends to the middle lock and remains there for three months; the child's navel is the confluence of veins, and all the woman's veins lead from it, through which its food and drink enter from those veins.

Then it descends to the lower lock and remains there for three months — making nine months in all. Then the woman goes into labor; with each contraction, a vein is severed from the child's navel, and the pain from this strikes her, while the child's hand is upon its navel until it falls to the ground with its hand outstretched; from that point onward, its sustenance comes through its mouth.

key_terms.أَقْفَال: Locks/compartments of the womb — a description of the three trimesters as distinct sections of the uterus, each housing the fetus for three months
key_terms.إِفَاضَة الْقِدَاح: Casting of divination arrows — pre-Islamic practice of distributing shares/lots by arrow; here used as a metaphor for God's distribution of destinies
key_terms.سَعِيد / شَقِيّ: Fortunate/miserable — theological terms for predestined states of the soul in Islamic theology (sa'ada/shaqawa)
key_terms.صُرَّة: Navel — the umbilical connection between mother and child, described as the confluence of all veins and the passage for nourishment

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about human creation and development in the womb?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) describes the cosmological process of human creation and development in the womb in response to Abu Hamza's question. The narrative begins with God's primordial determination of fate — distributing humanity like lots into the fortunate (Muslim) and the miserable (disbeliever) — then describes the angelic role in forming the embryo and determining sex, followed by a detailed account of fetal development through three womb 'locks' over nine months. This hadith reflects early Islamic cosmological and embryological understanding, merging theological concepts of divine predetermination with a detailed description of gestation, and would have been understood by its audience as a divinely revealed account of life's origins.
word_analysis: the woman has labor pains/is released

en.hubeali:
Muhamad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Muhammad Bin Al Fazeyl, from Abu Hamza who said, 
‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about the creation.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Blessed and High Created the creatures from clay, Effused by it like the effusion of the flint. So He<sup>azwj</sup> Extracted the Muslim and Made him as fortunate, and Make the Infidel as miserable.

So when the seed falls (into the womb), the two Angels meet it. So they caricature it, then say, ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! Male or female?’ So the Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Majestic is His<sup>azwj</sup> Majesty is Saying whatever that He<sup>azwj</sup> so Desires to. So they are both saying, ‘Blessed is Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the best of the creators’.

Then they place it in her belly. So it vibrates for nine days in every vein and join, and from it are three lock for the womb – a lock in its upper part from what follows to the top of the navel, from the right hand side; and another lock in the middle of it; and another lock in the lower part of the womb.
So, after nine days, they place him in the upper lock. So it remains in it for three months, during which the woman is hit by maliciousness, and the breathing (problems), and vomiting.

Then it descends to the middle lock. So it remains there for three months, during which (through) the navel of the child, its veins connect with the veins of the woman, all of these from which its food, and its drink enter, do so from these veins.

Then it descends to the lower lock, so it remains in it for three months. So these are the nine months. Then the woman undergoes pangs. So with each pain, a vein is cut off from the navel of the child. So that hits it with pain, and its hand is upon its navel until he falls to the ground, and his hand would be extended, so his sustenance from here on would be from its mouth’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu Hamzah who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the creation.

He (the Imam) said, ‘When Allah, most Blessed, most High, created the creation from clay He poured them as arrows are poured, took out the Muslim ones, made him fortunate and made the unbeliever wicked ones.

When the seed falls angels receive it and give it its shape then they ask, ‘O Lord, do You want it to be a male or female? ’ The Lord, most Majestic, most Glorious, then says whatever He wants.’ The two then say, ‘Blessed is Allah the best Creator.’

It then is placed inside her and it moves back and forth for nine days in every vein and joint. Inside from her to the womb there are three locks. One lock is for the upper side parallel to the bellybutton from the right side, the other lock is from the midsection and another lock is lower in the womb.
After nine days, it is placed in the upper lock where it remains for three months and at this time, the woman experiences disgust and nausea.

Thereafter it comes down to the middle lock and remains there for three months. The bellybutton of the child connects to a group of veins and all of the veins of the woman from which food enters as well as drinks by the way of these groups of veins.

Then the child descends down to the third lock where the child remains for another three months and this completes nine months. The woman then undergoes childlabor and with every pain a vein of the veins disconnect from the bellybutton of the child. When pain starts his hand rests on his bellybutton and he falls on the ground with his hands spread and thereafter his sustenance is by the way of his mouth.’”
